claims: NASA is targeting the Artemis II mission for launch on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day flight test.
The Artemis II mission marks the first human moon mission in over 50 years.
The Artemis II launch is set to lift off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The next launch date for Artemis II is as early as Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
The vehicle for Artemis II is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket carrying the Orion spacecraft.
The purpose of Artemis II is to test deep-space capabilities.
Artemis II is preparing for future long-term human exploration of the Moon.
The crew of Artemis II consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Launch viewing for Artemis II is available from the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
